en: Paṭisambhidāmagga 1 Mahāvagga 1.0 Matrix (Mātikā)
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
Wisdom regarding the application of the ear is knowledge consisting in what is heard.
Wisdom regarding restraint after having heard is knowledge consisting in virtue.
Wisdom in concentrating after having restrained oneself is knowledge consisting in the development of concentration.
Wisdom in discerning conditions is knowledge of the stability of phenomena.
Wisdom in defining past, future, and present phenomena by way of synthesis is knowledge of comprehension.
Wisdom in contemplating the change of presently arisen phenomena is knowledge of contemplation of rise and fall.
Wisdom in reflecting upon the object while contemplating its dissolution is knowledge of insight.
Wisdom in the manifestation of fear is knowledge of danger.
Wisdom as the desire for deliverance, reflective contemplation, and composure is knowledge of equanimity towards formations.
Wisdom regarding emergence and turning away from the external is change-of-lineage knowledge.
Wisdom regarding emergence and turning away from both is knowledge of the path.
Wisdom regarding the subsiding of the application [of the path] is knowledge of fruition.
Wisdom in contemplating the cutting off of the stream is knowledge of liberation.
Wisdom in seeing the states that have arisen at that time is knowledge of review.
Wisdom in the discernment of the internal is knowledge of the diversity of bases.
Wisdom in the discernment of the external is knowledge of the diversity of objects.
Wisdom in the discernment of conduct is knowledge of the diversity of conduct.
Wisdom in the discrimination of four things is knowledge of the diversity of planes.
Wisdom in the discrimination of nine things is knowledge of the diversity of phenomena.
Wisdom of direct knowledge is knowledge of the meaning of what has been known.
Wisdom as full understanding is knowledge in the sense of scrutinizing;
wisdom as abandoning is knowledge in the sense of relinquishing;
wisdom as development is knowledge in the sense of single function.
Wisdom as realization is knowledge in the sense of touching [the truth].
Wisdom regarding the diversity of meaning is knowledge in the analytical insight of meaning (atthapaṭisambhidā).
Wisdom regarding the diversity of phenomena is knowledge in the analytical insight of phenomena (dhammapaṭisambhidā).
Wisdom regarding the diversity of language is knowledge of the analytical knowledge of language (nirutti-paṭisambhidā).
Wisdom regarding the diversity of inspired expression is knowledge of the analytical knowledge of inspired expression (paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā).
Wisdom regarding the diversity of abidings is knowledge of the meaning of abiding (vihāraṭṭha).
Wisdom regarding the diversity of attainments is knowledge of the meaning of attainment.
Wisdom regarding the diversity of dwellings and attainments is knowledge of the meaning of dwelling and attainment.
Because of its purity through non-distraction, wisdom regarding the cutting off of the taints is knowledge of immediate concentration.
Wisdom regarding the predominance of vision, the attainment of peaceful abidings, and the inclination toward the sublime is knowledge of the abiding in the state free from conflict (*araṇavihāra*).

Wisdom consisting in mastery—due to being endowed with two powers, the subsiding of three formations, sixteen modes of conduct of knowledge, and nine modes of conduct of concentration—is knowledge of the attainment of cessation (*nirodhasamāpatti*).
Wisdom regarding the exhaustion of the process for one who is fully aware is knowledge of final Nibbāna (*parinibbāna*).
Wisdom regarding the complete eradication and cessation of all phenomena, and their non-reappearance, is knowledge in the sense of the equalizing of the head.
Wisdom regarding the exhaustion of various and diverse fires is knowledge in the sense of effacement.
Wisdom regarding the state of being unshrinking, resolute, and exerting effort is knowledge in the application of energy.
Wisdom as the manifestation of various phenomena is knowledge in the demonstration of meaning.
Wisdom as the unification of all phenomena and the penetration of their diversity and unity is knowledge of purification by vision.
Wisdom through having understood is knowledge of acceptance.
Wisdom by way of contact is knowledge of fathoming.
Wisdom in the act of bringing together is knowledge of abiding in a particular state.
Wisdom by way of predominance is knowledge of the turning away from perception.
Wisdom regarding diversity is knowledge of the turning away of the mind.
Wisdom regarding resolution is knowledge of the turning away of consciousness.
Wisdom regarding emptiness is knowledge of the turning away of knowledge.
Wisdom regarding the relinquishing of acquisitions is knowledge of turning away from liberation.
Wisdom regarding the state of suchness is knowledge of turning away from the truths.

Wisdom regarding the accomplishment of the body and mind as a single determination through the power of resolve—possessing the perception of ease and the perception of lightness—is knowledge of the various supernormal powers (*iddhividha*).
Wisdom that penetrates the various and manifold signs of sounds by means of the expansion of applied thought is the knowledge of the purification of the ear-element.

Wisdom that penetrates the movements of various and manifold consciousnesses by means of the clarity of the faculties due to the expansion of the three types of consciousness is the knowledge of penetration of minds.
Wisdom that penetrates phenomena as they arise through conditions by means of the expansion of various and manifold kamma is the knowledge of recollection of past lives.
Wisdom in the sense of seeing the signs of forms as diverse and unified by means of illumination is the knowledge of the divine eye.
Wisdom as mastery over the three faculties in sixty-four modes is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints.
Wisdom in the sense of full understanding is the knowledge of suffering.
Wisdom in the sense of abandoning is knowledge of the origin.
Wisdom in the sense of realization is knowledge of cessation.
Wisdom in the sense of development is knowledge of the path.
Knowledge of suffering;
knowledge of the origin of suffering;
knowledge of the cessation of suffering.
Knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of suffering;
knowledge of the analytical knowledge of meaning;
knowledge of the analytical knowledge of phenomena.
Knowledge of the analytical knowledge of language;
knowledge of the analytical knowledge of perspicuity;
knowledge of the degrees of the faculties of others.
Knowledge of the inclinations and underlying tendencies of beings;
knowledge of the twin miracle;
knowledge of the attainment of great compassion.
The knowledge of omniscience.
The unobstructed knowledge.
These are the seventy-seven knowledges.
Of these seventy-three knowledges, sixty-seven knowledges are shared with disciples;
six knowledges are not shared with disciples.
The Schedule is finished.
